propositions: The CLI write-command arg parsing uses hand-rolled loops with bespoke semantics (--assignee absent=None sentinel vs explicit empty-string clearing; --force command-specific following-token rules) that must be preserved when migrating to stdlib argparse without changing observable behavior.

The argparse refactor must disable defaults (add_help=False for dispatcher-served byte-exact --help; allow_abbrev=False for exact-token matching; parse_known_args for silent unknown-token skipping) and override error() to exit 1 with historical messages instead of argparse's exit 2.

transition._parse_flags must be retained as a thin argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple (reason, force_reason, close_class, caused_by, ref) for three external direct callers in tests; --force is inline-only (never consumes following token), force_reason is three-state (None=absent, ''=bare, '<r>'=reason), and --force-close is rejected with its bespoke message.

claim._parse_assignee transitions to argparse with None-vs-'' sentinel preserved (absent=>None=>default fallback, ''=>cleared); claim._parse_force handles command-specific following-token rules explicitly (bare --force consumes next non-option token else '(no reason given)').

The complexity-baseline.json entry for transition._parse_flags must be drained after the refactor drops it below the max-complexity threshold, and all existing CLI interface tests (incl. direct-caller unit tests) must pass unchanged with proper exit codes (1 for errors, 10 for ConcurrencyError).
